ABSTRACT
Literature reports indicate that existing synthesis methods for leveling agents
often sufer from complex procedures, high environmental burden, challenging
purification processes, and insuficient via filling eficiency. To address these
limitations, a novel leveling agent (CDT) was synthesized using environmentally
friendly materials through a simplified, cost-efective process that eliminates the
need for post-synthesis purification. This study systematically investigates the
influence of CDT on blind via filling performance in an acidic copper sulfate plat-
ing bath containing polyethylene glycol (PEG), bis(3-sulfopropyl) disulfide (SPS),
and chloride ions. The chemical structure of CDT was characterized by Fourier-
transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR),
and gel permeation chromatography (GPC). Quantum chemical calculations
and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations revealed that CDT exhibits stronger
adsorption on copper surfaces compared to conventional leveling agents. Elec-
trochemical measurements confirmed its ability to suppress copper deposition
and helped determine the optimal working concentration of CDT. Electroplat-
ing experiments further demonstrated CDT’s capability to achieve superfilling,
indicating its suitability for printed circuit board (PCB) manufacturing. Scan-
ning electron microscopy (SEM) results corroborated the validity of the optimal
concentration established by electrochemical tests. Finally, X-ray photoelectron
spectroscopy (XPS) confirmed strong interfacial interactions between CDT and
the copper surface. These findings collectively suggest that CDT is a highly prom-
ising candidate for advanced leveling agent applications.

1 Introduction
Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs) are indispensable com-
ponents in modern daily life. As current electronic
devices trend toward lighter, thinner, and smaller
designs, PCB technology is correspondingly evolving
toward multi-layer and high-density configurations. In
the PCB manufacturing industry, blind via technology
plays a crucial role as it facilitates conductive connec-
tions between the layers of multi-layer circuit boards.
Therefore, the metallization technology for blind vias
is particularly critical in this rapidly advancing field
To meet the high-performance demands of current
electronic devices, copper electroplating in blind vias
must achieve flawless filling without cracks and gaps.
This typically involves superfilling or botom-up fill-
ing techniques, where superfilling refers to a deposi-
tion process during electroplating in which the copper
deposition rate at the botom of the blind vias is signif-
icantly higher than at the opening and surface, thereby
achieving perfect filling of the vias [5]. To accomplish
superfilling, an acidic copper sulfate system is com
monly used in industrial applications. In this system,
the choice of additives is crucial, primarily including
accelerators, suppressors, and leveling agents. Accel-
erators, usually sulfur-containing organic compounds,
adsorb on the electrode surface, refine the copper crys-
tal structure, and promote copper nucleation. Their
primary function is to combine with chloride ions to
achieve depolarization, thus increasing the cathodic
current density [6–9]. The most widely studied and
used accelerators include SPS and MPS [10, 11]. Sup
pressors, such as polyether polymers (e.g., PEG and
PPG) [12–14], mainly inhibit the deposition of copper
during electroplating by adsorbing on the surface of
the plated parts and preventing the difusion of
{ \mathrm { C u } } ^ { 2 + }
[15–17]. In systems containing both accelerators and
suppressors, the role of leveling agents is indispensa-
ble. Leveling agents typically include certain nitrogen-
containing organic compounds [18, 19], such as the
dye-type leveling agents JGB [20], DB [18], ABPV [21,
22], and heterocyclic non-dye leveling agents such
as 2-amino-4-methylbenzothiazole [23] (AMBT) and
2-mercaptopyridine [24, 25] (2-MP). Their main func
tion is to work synergistically with suppressors to
inhibit copper deposition on the surface of the plated
parts, optimize current density distribution, enhance
filling eficiency, and thereby prevent premature hole
sealing that leads to voids [25–30]. Although the most
efective leveling agents are often commercial secrets,
high costs and poor environmental friendliness in the
market make the development of new leveling agents
both time-consuming and labor-intensive. Conse-
quently, to date, only a few superfilling leveling agents
have been specifically reported [31–33].
The importance of leveling agents in superfill-
ing copper electroplating has been corroborated by
numerous researchers. Literatures [34, 35] frequently
mention Janus Green B (JGB) as an efective leveling
agent that not only enhances the fill rate of blind
vias but also reduces the issue of protrusions during
filling. Myung Hyun Lee and other researchers [36]
synthesized a leveling agent containing two quater-
nary ammonium groups and hexaglycerol, which
successfully achieved seamless and void-free filling
of blind vias. Xu and colleagues [29] designed and
synthesized quaternary ammonium salts of diketo-
pyrrolopyrrole (DPP) with various aryl substitu-
ents. Additionally, Kim and others [37] developed
a choline-based leveling agent, 1,5-bis(2-N,N,N-
trimethylaminoethyl) pentanedioate diiodide, used
as a modulator in copper electroplating solutions.
Meanwhile, TCA [23] and DMP [38] have also been
reported as potential leveling agents. Their synthesis
processes are complex, the purification is challeng-
ing, and the raw material costs are high, all factors
that are unfavorable for industrial production.
This study, based on a comprehensive analysis of
existing literature, aims to develop a novel super-
filling leveling agent. During the synthesis process,
dimethylimidazole, imidazole, and 1,4-butanediol
diglycidyl ether were selected as raw materials, and
a detailed characterization of the organic structure of
the resulting leveling agent was performed. By inte-
grating quantum chemical calculations and molecu-
lar dynamics simulations, this research thoroughly
analyzed active sites and adsorption behaviors to
elucidate the interaction mechanisms between the
organic molecules and the copper surface. Further-
more, the filling mechanism of the leveling agent was
investigated using theoretical calculations, electro-
chemical measurements, and techniques such as
Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) and X-ray Pho-
toelectron Spectroscopy (XPS). Additionally, electro-
plating experiments were conducted to validate the
filling eficacy of the leveling agent and confirm its
suitability for specific requirements in Printed Cir-
cuit Board (PCB) applications.

3.5 Efects of CDT on deposit morphology
The influence of different concentrations of CDT
on the surface morphology of copper is depicted in
Fig. 12. In the absence of CDT in the plating solution,
the copper plating surface exhibits a rough, blocky,
and distinctly porous appearance. Conversely, com-
pared to the CDT-free condition, the addition of vary-
ing concentrations of CDT to the plating solution
significantly improves the surface morphology of the
copper plating (Figs. 12b–h). The formation of smooth
planes is due to the modification of the plating layer
after adding CDT, which initiates crystal refinement.
However, when the CDT concentration is increased to
5 mg/L, a proliferation of small blocky crystals appears
on the copper surface, becoming denser with increas-
ing concentrations of CDT. These results indicate that
CDT demonstrates its leveling capability efectively
within a certain concentration range, but as the con-
centration of the leveling agent increases, the syner-
gistic interactions among the additives are disrupted.
Similar results have been reported in copper electro-
depositing studies [18, 21].

4 Conclusions
In summary, we have selected the nitrogen-hetero-
cyclic compound CDT as an electroplating leveling
agent for copper micro-via filling. The synthesis of
CDT was successfully confirmed by infrared, hydro-
gen nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, and
gel permeation chromatography results. Quantum
chemical simulations suggest that CDT possesses
the potential to occupy metal vacant orbitals for
adsorption. Moreover, molecular dynamics simu-
lations indicate that CDT exhibits strong affinity
for copper surfaces. Electrochemical tests revealed
that the optimal working concentration of CDT is
5 mg/L. Chronopotentiometric measurements further
demonstrated that CDT can synergistically suppress
copper deposition when combined with other addi-
tives, exhibiting a potential diference as high as
20 mV, which indicates its strong inhibitory efect on
copper electrodeposition. Electroplating tests show
that the best plating results occur at a concentration
of 5 mg/L, consistent with electrochemical findings.
Field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-
SEM) results showed that CDT can refine copper
grain structures within an appropriate concentration
range; however, when the concentration exceeds the
optimal level, crystal agglomeration reoccurs. X-ray
photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) confirmed the
efective adsorption of CDT on the copper surface,
and the strong interaction between them provides
a foundation for the suppression of copper deposi-
tion. Collectively, our research conclusively proves
that CDT is a promising leveling agent for copper
micro-via filling, providing theoretical guidance for
the discovery and improvement of electroplating
technologies for micro-via filling.
